Subject: Draft redline language for AceroHealth

1) Post-reconciliation price ceiling
Proposed clause: "Notwithstanding any adjustments arising from usage reconciliation, credits, or chargebacks (including burst or overage credits), Redwood shall ensure that the effective per-unit price charged to Customer for any billing quarter shall not exceed the maximum unit price (ceiling) set forth in the Pricing Exhibit for that quarter. Any reconciliation that would otherwise result in an effective per-unit charge above the ceiling shall be offset by a pro-rated credit to Customer such that the effective per-unit price is equal to, but does not exceed, the stated ceiling. Credits shall be applied on the invoice immediately following such reconciliation."

Rationale: explicit cap protects against mechanical interactions between burst credits and volume true-ups. Keeps invoice flow simple (credit on next invoice).

2) Packaging rebucketing protection
Proposed clause: "Redwood may, with thirty (30) days' prior written notice, modify the packaging or SKU mapping applicable to the Services for operational reasons; provided, however, that in the event such modification results in Customer's Committed Units being assigned to a higher-priced packaging tier, Redwood shall provide Customer a pro-rated credit for the term remaining in the applicable Commitment Period. The credit shall be calculated as (A) the difference between the applicable unit price under the new packaging tier and the unit price Customer would have paid under the prior packaging tier, multiplied by (B) the Customer's committed units impacted, pro-rated for the remainder of the Commitment Period. The parties agree to a good-faith mapping exercise to identify impacted commitment quantities prior to any final rebucketing."

Rationale: preserves Redwood's ability to optimize packaging while protecting the customer's committed economics. We should include a worked example in the order schedule (see attachment packaging_map_v2.xlsx).

3) True-up window and audit carveout
Proposed clause: "Unless otherwise agreed, Customer shall reconcile actual usage within one hundred twenty (120) days following the end of each calendar quarter. If Customer timely notifies Redwood of a dispute related to a reconciliation, Redwood shall not apply the disputed portion of any adjustments until the dispute is resolved; provided that any undisputed amounts remain payable in accordance with the invoice terms."

Please confirm if the worked example in packaging_map_v2.xlsx is acceptable. Ben / Kimberly — any operational or revenue recognition implications?

-Marissa
